questions.q: How does air pressure produce winds?
answer: Air exerts pressure in all directions, and differences in this pressure set the air in motion as wind.

answer.text: When air is heated it becomes lighter and rises, leaving an area of low pressure below. Cooler, denser air sinks and creates high pressure. Air then moves from the region of high pressure to the region of low pressure, and this moving air is wind.

The Earth is heated unevenly — the equator more than the poles, and land differently from the sea. This uneven heating creates pressure differences that drive winds, including the land and sea breezes and the seasonal monsoon.

answer: The greater the difference in pressure, the stronger the wind that blows.

questions.q: What is a cyclone, and how can people stay safe from it?

answer.text: A cyclone is a large, powerful storm that forms over warm seas. It has a region of very low pressure at its centre, called the eye, around which violent winds spin, bringing heavy rain and high waves. Such storms are called hurricanes in the Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific.

The India Meteorological Department tracks cyclones and issues early warnings. On receiving a warning, people in coastal areas move to cyclone shelters or safe buildings, store food and water, and stay away from the sea. Good preparedness — early warnings, sturdy shelters and timely evacuation — has greatly reduced the loss of life from cyclones.
